newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah softens on short-covering.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah softens on short-covering.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah softened against the dollar in late trading on Friday on short-covering from offshore operators, dealers said.
They said volume was a little thin, with late short dollar covering from London operators sending the rupiah break the 2,430 resistance level.

The dollar-rupiah rates were trapped in a narrow range between 2,429.0 and 2,430.5 on Friday. Spot rupiah was last at 2,430.0/30.5 at 0900 GMT. Tomorrow and today rupiah closed at 2,429.75/30.25 and 2,428.65/29.00, respectively.
"It's a slow day. We saw some short-covering in the late afternoon and sustained firm swap rates," one dealer said.

Dealers said President Suharto's minor cabinet reshuffle did not have any impact on the financial markets. Suharto replaced Information Minister Harmoko with retiring army chief of staff General Hartono.
Harmoko becomes minister for special affairs.

Dealers said the move came as a surprise, but it had no implication on the foreign exchange market. They said what the market was waiting for was whether the United Development Party (PPP) would accept the last week's election results.
The party was scheduled to make a decision on Friday but has delayed it as the party's meeting was still proceeding and no final decision had been reached so far.
Operators were worried of possible post-election violence if the party declined to accept the results because it had claimed there were widespread irregularities at the election.
Golkar took over 74 percent of the national vote.
Dealers said liquidity was slightly tighter than Thursday, helping overnight money to hover at around 11.0 percent.
Overnight swap was at 0.80/1.10 points and tom/next at 0.15/0.20 points.
Dealers said offshore players continued to maintain long forward positions on fears that the central bank would resort to measures taken by the Thai authorities.
The Thai central bank had asked operators to stop quoting tom/next to offshore players to close their funding sources.
However, Bank Indonesia had denied plans for such a move for now. But offshore operators did not want to take risks after being squeezed heavily in the Thai market.
They extended their long forward positions, going long on the rupiah in the forward market and keeping swap rates high.
One-month swaps were at 12.00/12.75, two at 26.50/27.25, three at 38.5/39.5 and six at 78.0/79.0 points.
The central bank raised its intervention band by one point to 2,419/2,611 and its conversion band also by one point to 2,419/2,467 on Friday.
